ownership_reason: EarthMoversDistance.compute (E) is one delegation to EnumeratedDistribution.transportCost (H1), whose javadoc says it returns exactly Sum.carriedCost(a, b, Frequency.occupiedBins(a, b)), and that is its whole body. Frequency.occupiedBins (H2) is documented to return, in increasing order, exactly the indices i < a.length with a[i] != 0 or b[i] != 0, leaving out bins that are empty in both histograms. On the trigger histograms {0.5,0,0,0.5,0,0} and {0,0,0.5,0,0,0.5} it returns {0,2,3,5}, as documented; the new FrequencyTest.testNonEmptyPositions passes on the variant and pins this contract. Sum.carriedCost (H3, the gold) is documented to visit the listed bins with a running surplus (a[j] + surplus) - b[j], to carry that surplus from bin j to the next listed bin (or to a.length after the last one), and to charge |surplus| * (next - j), because unlisted bins are empty and are only crossed. Its code adds |surplus| once per listed bin and drops the factor (next - j). The two half-unit surpluses each travel two unit steps (bin 0 to 2 and bin 3 to 5), so each is charged 0.5 instead of 1.0. The trigger therefore gets 1.0 instead of 2.0, and 2.0 is the textbook earth mover's distance for these histograms (0.5 moved two bins, twice). The existing EarthMoversDistanceTest cases (test, testZero, testZero2) pass on the variant: their histograms have no bin that is empty in both while a surplus crosses it, so every gap is one step. They pin the E/H1/H2/H3 composition on dense input. E and H1 do exactly what their javadoc says (delegate or compose) and promise nothing about distance weighting. Restoring the (next - j) factor and its next line in carriedCost alone makes the trigger and the full suite pass. Making occupiedBins list every bin would also make the trigger pass, but it contradicts occupiedBins' documented contract and fails FrequencyTest.testNonEmptyPositions (declared G9 edit). Swapping the argument order in E or H1, or keying occupancy on one histogram, does not make the trigger pass.

compensating.why: one-line H2 edit: occupiedBins lists every bin, empty or not, so the unit-step charge per listed bin covers the gaps
one-line H2 edit: occupiedBins keys occupancy on the first histogram only
